item.title: Trump officials cut political interference ban after unusual Census Bureau report
item.description: After the Census Bureau issued a report tied to a Trump-aligned think tank, the bureau's parent agency cut language banning political interference from its scientific integrity policy, NPR learned.
item.content:encoded:
After the Census Bureau issued a report tied to a Trump-aligned think tank, the bureau's parent agency cut language banning political interference from its scientific integrity policy, NPR learned.

(Image credit: Michael Zamora)

item.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. famine alert system that Trump shut down, then reopened
item.description: The highly regarded FEWS NET network stopped posting data on Afghanistan, Somalia and Yemen -- then says it will start posting again in September. What's the reason for this back-and-forth?
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Kalshi bans former congressman George Santos for life after State of the Union trades
item.description: Kalshi says Santos did not cooperate with its investigation into bets he placed on his own attendance at the State of the Union. The company also fined the disgraced congressman more than $71,000.

item.title: The U.S. sues Amazon again
item.description: Federal regulators and 22 states allege that the tech giant made billions by manipulating how much brands and sellers paid for ads on its platform.

item.title: Paperwork, lines, hours on hold: There's a 'Time Tax' on Americans who need help most
item.description: Annie Lowrey explores the administrative burdens people face applying for government benefits. It's not just about wasted time: "When the government treats us like this, we don't trust it," she says.

item.title: Lionel Messi says he's retiring from playing internationally for Argentina
item.description: The soccer star is ending 21 years of Argentine national-team duty but will continue to play at club level with Inter Miami in U.S. Major League Soccer.

item.description: A group of the country's private sector power producers says Nepali authorities lost crucial time in rescuing hundreds of people trapped in hydropower tunnels.

item.title: U.S., Venezuela strike oil deal. And, the staggering hidden toll of U.S. heat deaths
item.description: The U.S. and Venezuela have entered into an oil deal. And, NPR spent two years tracking heat-related deaths and found that people in the U.S. are dying from heat more than the official counts show.

item.title: Russia's jet-powered drones bring empty Kyiv supermarket shelves and rattle Ukrainians
item.description: Russian forces relentlessly battered Kyiv and cities in the region around the Ukrainian capital for a fifth straight day, leaving some supermarket shelves bare after repeated strikes on warehouses.

item.title: Attacks flare between the U.S. and Iran after a monthlong pause
item.description: U.S. threats erupt into attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran retaliates against U.S. targets in the United Arab Emirates and Jordan in the first exchange of fire since July 29.
